correctness.rationale: For independent fixed positive Poisson rates and n≥2, the homogeneous maximum mass factors f_k=p_b(k)H_k. Monotone log increments of the Poisson cumulative masses imply synchronized H_k log concavity; the Poisson factorial ratio converts it to all k≥1 ULC. For unequal rates, exact product-CDF telescoping yields h_k=f_k/p_b(k)=m+s·exp(b−a)(a/b)^k+o((a/b)^k) where a<b are top distinct rates. Consequently (h_k²−h_{k−1}h_{k+1})/(a/b)^k→−m s exp(b−a)(b−a)²/(ab)<0 and all sufficiently large k violate ULC. Independently recomputed exact rational Poisson CDF masses show first (1,2) violation at k=4 with scaled defect −17/360 and confirm finite homogeneous/heterogeneous samples, not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: Badiella–del Castillo–Puig (2023) prove preservation of ULC for independent identically distributed discrete order statistics: homogeneous sufficiency is known. Chowdhury–Kundu–Mishra (2021) compare heterogeneous Poisson order statistics by stochastic majorization, not this discrete curvature, and Yu treats distributional relative log-concavity. The novel asserted part is exact necessity for any heterogeneity plus its second-highest-rate tail constant; no covering result found in actual comparisons. Badiella full primary PDF was access-blocked, documented as residual risk, not automatically a failure.
